Patrick Wahome, who has organised protests in Nanyuki against the centre, told Reuters on Tuesday the man died from a gunshot wound to the head. Reporters from the agency saw his body lying motionless in a police van with a large head wound.

Min Zin was suspected of “engaging in espionage activities that endanger China’s national security,” China’s ministry of foreign affairs spokesperson, Lin Jian, said on Friday.

euronews.description: Japan is sharing decades of disaster management expertise with Vietnam through infrastructure, education and early warning projects backed by The Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) and UNESCO.

euronews.title: SpaceX makes its Nasdaq debut after the largest public offering in history
euronews.description: Elon Musk's SpaceX began trading on the Nasdaq this Friday under the ticker SPCX, following a record $75bn (€65bn) capital raise that valued the AI and space firm at about $1.78 trillion (€1.54trn).

euronews.title: New France-Ireland ferry revives Boulogne's international links
euronews.description: A new overnight service linking Cork and Boulogne-sur-Mer has begun operations, restoring international passenger ferries to the northern French port for the first time in 15 years and offering travellers another route that avoids the UK.

euronews.title: Belgian driver convicted of murder over carnival car crash that killed seven people
euronews.description: The trial was heard in a special hall to accommodate nearly 200 civil parties taking part. The civil claimants include some who are disabled for life and the relatives of those who died.

euronews.title: From Florence to Crete: 11 European hotels among the world’s best new stays
euronews.description: From restored palaces in Rome and Bucharest to countryside retreats in Devon and Crete, travel magazine Afar has unveiled its annual ranking of the world's best new and revamped hotels - with 11 standout properties in Europe making the cut.

euronews.title: EMYA 2026: Which museum will be named Europe’s best?
euronews.description: Thirty-four nominees are eyeing this year’s European Museum of the Year Award - from Portugal and Estonia to Türkiye and the United Kingdom. Here are some of the museums competing for the right to be called Europe's best museum of 2026.

euronews.title: Any change to EU protection scheme for Ukrainians should be 'gradual', UNHCR deputy chief says
euronews.description: Kelly Clements tells Euronews that any planned changes to EU protections for Ukrainian refugees should be carried out "very gradually", as some EU capitals push for excluding military-age men from the scheme.

euronews.title: Israel: Tel Aviv pride marchers push for LGBTQ+ equality amid tensions and war
euronews.description: Thousands of people joined the Tel Aviv Pride parade on 12 June, filling the city's seafront with rainbow flags, music and calls for greater LGBTQ+ rights in a region where equality remains limited.

euronews.title: The path to SAFE II: inside the struggle to revamp Europe's defence financing tool
euronews.description: EU policymakers are weighing a SAFE II defence financing tool, with Eastern-flank states pushing for grants over loans. But the final SAFE I uptake, the development of the European defence industry, Ukraine's battlefield-driven tech edge and shifting warfare scenarios are shaping what comes next.

euronews.title: US withdraws long-range military capabilities from NATO
euronews.description: The move comes at a particularly tense moment, with US Donald Trump increasingly angry at NATO allies over their refusal to join his war on Iran.

euronews.title: EU energy ministers eye jet fuel reserves as Strait of Hormuz crisis threatens supply
euronews.description: With the peak summer season drawing near, EU energy ministers are wary that jet fuel supply may be further strained, even as analysts see "sharp movement" towards greater jet fuel production within European refineries.

euronews.title: Washington plans to slash fighter jets and warships to NATO in Europe, US media report
euronews.description: The reported cutbacks come as European nations race to bolster their defence capacities since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022 sparked fears that Moscow could attack a NATO country.

euronews.title: Pope urges 'reciprocal' integration between migrants and host countries
euronews.description: During his visit to Tenerife, the pontiff called for integration based on rights and duties, urging migrants to learn the language, obey the law and join in community life.

euronews.title: What to know about the EU's new migration and asylum reforms as they come into effect
euronews.description: The bloc’s new migration rules take effect on Friday after months of political wrangling. Here are the changes that are now in force.

euronews.title: ‘Land of the fulfilled  farmers’: Why the grass seems to grow greener in Austria
euronews.description: Austria has repeatedly been acknowledged as a success story in the intergenerational renewal of its farming sector. A combination of hard work at family-run farms, strong public support, qualitative professional training and engaged consumers is revitalizing entire rural communities.

rfi.title: Resumption of $20bn Cabo Delgado gas project reignites both hope and resentment
rfi.description: The resumption of one of the world's biggest gas projects by French energy giant TotalEnergies, after a five-year suspension following a deadly jihadist attack, has raised hopes of jobs and prosperity in northern Mozambique. But this second instalment of Mozambique Exposed – an investigation coordinated by Forbidden Stories, to which RFI contributed – questions whether the country's vast gas wealth will benefit local communities.

rfi.title: Paris no longer carries the load as audit backs asylum redistribution plan
rfi.description: France's system for moving asylum seekers from the Paris region to other parts of the country has helped ease pressure on accommodation, but is not being used to its full potential and remains unevenly applied, according to the country's public spending watchdog.

rfi.title: What's in the landmark EU migration reform hardening border protections?
rfi.description: A major reform of European migration rules aimed at hardening border procedures and overhauling the asylum process comes into force on Friday.

rfi.title: Israeli and Palestinian groups urge action on two-state solution in Paris
rfi.description: Israeli and Palestinian civil society groups will meet in Paris on Friday to urge the international community not to abandon a two-state solution, as France seeks to keep the issue on the agenda amid the ongoing war in the Middle East.

rfi.title: Sudan rights groups blame RSF paramilitary for drone strikes that hit civilians
rfi.description: Drone strikes blamed on the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) have killed at least 23 civilians and wounded 19 others in the Sudanese city of El-Obeid, local monitoring groups have said, as the use of armed drones continues to spread across the country in its more than three-year war.

rfi.title: British art 'giant' David Hockney dies aged 88
rfi.description: British artist David Hockney, one of the most influential and defining figures in contemporary art, whose paintings captured the world in brilliant colour, has died aged 88, his publicist announced Friday.

rfi.title: Two French cities impose curfews for under-16s during World Cup
rfi.description: The mayors of Toulouse and Clermont-Ferrand are imposing nighttime curfews on children under 16 during the 2026 World Cup. They say the move is aimed at preventing the violent unrest seen after Paris Saint-Germain's Champions League victory last month.

rfi.title: Rise in adulterated cannabis in France, as edible CBD ban shakes industry
rfi.description: Cannabis use in France is once again under scrutiny, with a drugs monitor reporting a sharp rise in adulterated products on the illegal market, and risky new products entering the legal CBD market. To address the issue of mislabelled products, France has banned edible CBD products, raising concerns in the cannabis industry.

rfi.title: Ebola outbreak spreads in DRC as misinformation hampers response
rfi.description: Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have launched an online campaign to tackle growing mistrust surrounding a deadly Ebola outbreak. The World Health Organization (WHO) says misinformation is hampering efforts to contain the haemorrhagic fever, which broke out in the eastern province of Ituri on 15 May.

rfi.title: Mexico brush past ill-disciplined South Africa to launch World Cup party
rfi.description: Mexico's Julian Quinones and Raul Jimenez punished an indisciplined South Africa on Thursday night in the opening match of the 2026 World Cup.

rfi.title: Man linked to Dominique Pelicot on trial accused of drugging and raping partner
rfi.description: A man with ties to convicted French mass rapist Dominique Pelicot is on trial in Lyon, accused of drugging and raping his partner while filming the assaults and streaming them online.

rfi.title: Children in danger 'not heard' in France, rights lawyer warns after Lyhanna death
rfi.description: The abduction and killing of 11-year-old French schoolgirl Lyhanna has catapaulted child protection to the top of France's political agenda – with President Emmanuel Macron on Wednesday calling for full accountability and the government pledging full transparency. As investigators examine possible failures by the justice system, child rights lawyer Dominique Attias tells RFI professionals have been warning for years that vulnerable children are not being protected.

rfi.title: Killing of gay man to be investigated as homophobic crime following protests
rfi.description: Police investigating the murder of a young gay man in the eastern French city of Metz have said the case will now be treated as a homophobic crime, after protestations from rights groups and politicians.

rfi.title: RFI denounces violation of press freedom after French reporter barred by Israel
rfi.description: RFI has condemned Israel's decision to refuse entry to journalist Alice Froussard, describing the move as "an obstacle to press freedom". Froussard, who reports on the Israeli-Palestinian conflict for French media, including RFI, was turned away on arrival at Tel Aviv airport and sent back without explanation.

rfi.title: Climate report shows 1.5C limit on global warming will be breached by 2030
rfi.description: Human-induced global warming is on track to reach 1.5C around 2030, a group of leading scientists said on Thursday.

rfi.title: Fifa grants World Cup accreditation to jailed French journalist Christophe Gleizes
rfi.description: In a move hailed by press freedom campaigners as an important gesture of solidarity, Fifa has issued World Cup accreditation to French sports journalist Christophe Gleizes, who has been detained in Algeria for more than a year.

rfi.title: French pop star Patrick Bruel charged with rape and sexual assault
rfi.description: French singer and actor Patrick Bruel has been charged with rape, attempted rape, sexual assault and sexual harassment, prosecutors said on Wednesday, in a case that now involves accusations by more than 20 women.

rfi.title: Amnesty accuses Israel of ‘ethnic cleansing’ of West Bank Bedouin communities
rfi.description: Amnesty International has accused Israel of carrying out what it described as a state-led campaign of “ethnic cleansing” against Bedouin and herding communities in the occupied West Bank, saying the measures were intended to accelerate the annexation of Palestinian territory.

lemonde.title: Avec l’introduction en Bourse démesurée de SpaceX, la fortune d’Elon Musk atteint 1 000 milliards de dollars
lemonde.description: L’action SpaceX a bondi de 18 % lors de ses premiers échanges au Nasdaq, à Wall Street, vendredi 12 juin, valorisant la firme à plus de 2000 milliards de dollars. La société, toujours déficitaire et dont le chiffre d’affaires reste modeste, a réussi son pari de vendre aux investisseurs les projets irréalistes de son fondateur.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre au Moyen-Orient : Donald Trump dément les termes de l’accord avec Téhéran tels qu’ils ont été rapportés par les médias iraniens
lemonde.description: Le président américain a par ailleurs vivement condamné ce qu’il présente comme une tentative d’attaque de drones iranienne contre des navires indiens quittant le détroit d’Ormuz, dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi.

lemonde.title: Derrière l’opération d’ingérence contre LFI lors des municipales, un insaisissable commanditaire
lemonde.description: Les autorités françaises ont publié des informations accréditant l’implication d’une officine israélienne, Blackcore. Selon les informations du « Monde », d’autres sociétés pourraient avoir joué un rôle. Un maquis de sous-traitants qui complique l’identification du donneur d’ordres.

lemonde.title: Après la une prorusse du « JDNews », le délicat grand écart du RN
lemonde.description: Jordan Bardella, le président du parti d’extrême droite, balaie les arguments de Philippe de Villiers en faveur de la Russie, tout en maintenant un déplacement prévu au Puy du Fou, le parc d’attractions de la tête d’affiche du groupe de Vincent Bolloré.

lemonde.title: Jean-Michel Aulas, sous pression après l’affaire d’abus sexuel non dénoncée, se retire de la gouvernance de son groupe municipal à Lyon
lemonde.description: A la métropole comme à la ville, les groupes politiques constitués autour de Jean-Michel Aulas se déchirent à cause de l’affaire d’abus sexuel sous soumission chimique, signalée durant la campagne électorale. Une majorité d’élus de tous bords lui reproche le manque de soutien à la victime.

lemonde.title: Dylan Robert, ancien acteur césarisé, soupçonné d’extorsion à l’égard d’un rappeur marseillais depuis sa prison
lemonde.description: Le meilleur espoir masculin pour « Shéhérazade », déjà mis en cause dans des affaires criminelles, a été mis en examen le 9 juin pour « extorsion en bande organisée » dans le cadre d’une enquête du Parquet national anticriminalité organisée ouverte en 2026.

lemonde.title: EN DIRECT, guerre en Ukraine : un tir du missile balistique russe Orechnik redouté par l’armée de l’air ukrainienne dans les prochaines vingt-quatre heures
lemonde.description: La Russie a frappé à trois reprises avec l’Orechnik, à la fin 2024, début 2026 et le 24 mai. A chaque fois, le missile ne portait pas de charge nucléaire. Un quatrième Orechnik s’est écrasé sur une agglomération de l’autoproclamée « république populaire de Donetsk », le 23 mai.

lemonde.title: Présidentielle 2027 : Raphaël Glucksmann affirme n’avoir « aucun doute » sur le fait de s’allier avec le PS
lemonde.description: Le dirigeant de Place publique, probable candidat à la présidentielle, en meeting samedi 13 juin, dit ne pas imaginer « une seconde une campagne séparée des militants socialistes ».

lemonde.title: Coupe du monde 2026 : de la « haine » à un amour raisonné, le football masculin sort progressivement de l’ombre aux Etats-Unis
lemonde.description: Longtemps considéré comme un sport de femmes, le soccer est de plus en plus suivi et pratiqué par des hommes outre-Atlantique. Un beau parcours de la sélection, lors du deuxième Mondial organisé à domicile, pourrait achever de convaincre les réticents.

lemonde.title: Les questions que vous n’avez jamais posées à vos parents
lemonde.description: S’il n’est pas toujours facile d’oser questionner ses parents, arrive le jour où leur disparition rend la chose impossible. Vous avez confié vos espoirs et vos regrets à Clara Georges pour sa newsletter « Darons daronnes ».

lemonde.title: Affaire de la « sextape » : cinq ans de prison, dont trois ferme, requis en appel contre l’ancien maire de Saint-Etienne
lemonde.description: L’ancien édile de 53 ans, qui nie farouchement toute implication dans cette affaire depuis sa révélation par « Médiapart » en 2022, a déjà passé deux mois derrière les barreaux cet hiver en exécution provisoire d’une peine de cinq ans, dont quatre ferme.

lemonde.title: Affaire Robert Boulin : le dossier sur la mort de l’ancien ministre de Valéry Giscard d’Estaing relancé au pôle « cold cases » de Nanterre
lemonde.description: Le 30 octobre 1979, le corps sans vie de ce gaulliste historique, perçu comme un potentiel premier ministre, était retrouvé dans un étang de Rambouillet (Yvelines). La famille dénonce plusieurs manquements lors de l’enquête.

lemonde.title: Le fondateur de FTX, Sam Bankman-Fried, voit sa peine de vingt-cinq ans de prison confirmée en appel
lemonde.description: Agé de 34 ans et actuellement en détention, celui qui a longtemps été considéré comme un petit génie des cryptomonnaies a été reconnu coupable de fraude, d’association de malfaiteurs et de blanchiment d’argent.

lemonde.title: Méthane : l’UE en passe d’assouplir ses règles au nom de la sécurité énergétique
lemonde.description: Le règlement de l’Union européenne visant à lutter contre les émissions de ce puissant gaz à effet de serre, principal composant du gaz naturel, est vigoureusement contesté par les Etats-Unis comme par l’industrie fossile.

lemonde.title: Le physicien Etienne Klein sanctionné par son université pour plagiats
lemonde.description: En raison de nombreux passages plagiés dans le texte de sa thèse de philosophie des sciences soutenue en 1999, l’université Paris Cité a décidé de lui retirer son doctorat. Le CEA, son employeur, dit « agir en conséquence ».

lemonde.title: Que regarder ce soir à la TV ? « The Hack », sur Arte.tv
lemonde.description: David Tennant se glisse dans la peau du journaliste Nick Davies pour une minisérie pédagogique sur le scandale des années 2010 ayant conduit à la fermeture du tabloïd « News of the World » détenu par Rupert Murdoch.

france24fr.title: Introduction de SpaceX en bourse : l'opération qui bat tous les records
france24fr.description: C'est une opération sans équivalent dans l'histoire de la finance. L'entreprise spatiale californienne SpaceX – création et propriété d'Elon Musk – fait ses premiers pas sur le marché d'actions américain avec des chiffres stratosphériques : 555 millions d'actions et une valorisation estimée entre 1 765 et 2 000 milliards de dollars, soit près de cent fois le chiffre d'affaires de l'entreprise en 2025. Pourquoi un tel engouement ? Risque-t-on une bulle spatiale ?

france24fr.title: Edi Rama parle "d'ingérence iranienne" contre le projet immobilier des Trump
france24fr.description: Cette semaine, nous recevons Edi Rama, Premier ministre albanais. Il commente les manifestations qui secouent son pays contre la construction d'un complexe hôtelier de luxe lié à la famille Trump.

france24fr.title: Accord "imminent" avec l’Iran ? Trump brouille les pistes avec ses revirements incessants
france24fr.description: Après avoir affirmé la veille qu'un accord avec l'Iran pourrait être signé dans les prochains jours pour mettre fin à la guerre, Donald Trump a changé de ton vendredi, accusant Téhéran de mentir. Une séquence qui résume à elle seule les profondes incertitudes entourant les négociations et leurs chances d'aboutir après plus de quatre mois de conflit. Décryptage.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : le Maroc de Hakimi se prépare avant son match contre le Brésil
france24fr.description:
À moins de deux jours de son premier match contre le Brésil, le Maroc se prépare dans son camp de base à Basking Ridge, dans le New Jersey. La sélection a dû
 
essuyer plusieurs coups durs avec les forfaits de deux joueurs clés mais ses supporters restent optimistes. Crédit musique : George Van Dyk.

france24fr.title: Xénophobie en Afrique du Sud : un climat de peur qui s’accentue avant l’ultimatum du 30 juin
france24fr.description: Le Nigeria, le Ghana et le Malawi ont rapatrié ces derniers jours plusieurs centaines de ressortissants depuis l’Afrique du Sud, craignant pour leur sécurité après de violentes manifestations contre les immigrés. Un climat de peur entretenu par des groupes xénophobes qui exigent le départ des étrangers illégaux d'ici la fin du mois de juin.

france24fr.title: "Zeroers" : quand la Russie récompense la brutalité de ses commandants
france24fr.description: Le colonel Ramil Faskhoutdinov est devenu vendredi "héros de la Russie" à l’occasion de la fête nationale russe. Un honneur pour ce commandant accusé à de multiples reprises de brutalité extrême contre ses hommes et qui représente la figure du "zeroer", terme jargonneux désignant un chef militaire qui s’arroge un droit de vie et de mort sur les soldats qu’il commande.

france24fr.title: Arménie, le choix de l'Europe ?
france24fr.description: Quelle marge de manœuvre pour Nikol Pachinian après la victoire de son parti, Contrat civil, aux dernières législatives en Arménie ? Si la victoire consacre l'orientation impulsée par le Premier ministre depuis 2018, elle est vue par certains comme un défi à Moscou qui conserve quelques leviers de pression. Nikol Pachinian, qui s'est rapproché des Occidentaux, a cherché à régler le conflit avec l'Azerbaïdjan et à préserver ses liens avec la Russie tout en s'émancipant de Moscou. Les élections lé

france24fr.title: Des centres de retour pour migrants hors de l'UE : un pacte anti-migration ?
france24fr.description: La politique migratoire de l'Union européenne (UE) mise en œuvre en ce mois de juin se durcit. Après des années de débats, le Pacte asile et migration va s'appliquer. Cet ensemble législatif est censé instaurer une solidarité entre les Vingt-Sept pour répartir les demandeurs d'asile et aussi accélérer l'examen des dossiers en prévoyant un filtrage aux frontières extérieures de l'Union européenne dans des zones de transit.

france24fr.title: VSS : la France face aux dysfonctionnements de sa justice
france24fr.description: C'est une France sous le choc qui découvre l'ampleur des dysfonctionnements de sa justice. La mort de la petite Lyhanna, onze ans, a pris le pays aux tripes lorsque le profil du principal suspect a été connu… Jérôme Barella, père de famille "sans histoire" traînait en réalité plaintes et signalements à son encontre, pour attouchements et viols, depuis 2017 sans jamais avoir été convoqué par les autorités. La multiplication des témoignages de femmes contre Patrick Bruel arrive dans la même périod

france24fr.title: Îles Canaries : le pape Léon XIV rencontre des migrants
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV met en garde contre un "naufrage silencieux" qui menace les migrants après leur arrivée dans un nouveau pays, qualifiant l'indifférence mondiale face aux décès en mer d'"échec pour la famille humaine" lors d'une visite historique dans un centre d'accueil des îles Canaries.

france24fr.title: Mondial 2026 : par peur de violences, des villes françaises édictent des couvre-feux
france24fr.description: Par craintes de débordements après certaines rencontres considérées comme "à risque", de grandes villes comme Toulouse et Clermont-Ferrand ont prévu d'instaurer des couvre-feux pour les mineurs non accompagnés lors du Mondial. D'autres maires ne veulent pas de fan zones dans leurs communes.

france24fr.title: Les échappées de Kaboul : pédaler c’est résister
france24fr.description:
"Les Échappées de Kaboul" : le documentaire revient sur l'évacuation secrète de 41 cyclistes #afghanes après la prise de pouvoir des talibans en août 2021.
 
🚵‍♀️ Portées par un élan de solidarité d’ONG, de philanthropes, de personnalités politiques et sportives, 125 personnes ont pu fuir le pays dans des conditions extrêmes.
 
Un documentaire de Matteo Born et Alain Rimbert.

france24fr.title: Moyen-Orient : l’Iran évoque des progrès significatifs vers un accord avec Washington
france24fr.description: Téhéran se montre prudent mais affirme qu’une grande partie de l’accord avec Washington serait déjà finalisée. Le cessez-le-feu au Liban et le déblocage d’avoirs iraniens semblent avancer, mais les questions du nucléaire et du détroit d’Ormuz restent à régler, comme l'explique le correspondant de France 24 à Téhéran Siavosh Ghazi.

france24fr.title: Fin de la visite du Pape en Espagne placée sous le signe de la défense des migrants
france24fr.description: Le pape Léon XIV a achevé son voyage d’une semaine en Espagne par une visite aux îles Canaries, principale porte d’entrée des migrants vers l’Europe. Tout au long de son déplacement, il a plaidé pour un accueil digne des migrants, dénonçant l’indifférence face aux drames migratoires et appelant à davantage de solidarité. Les précisions de Victoria David, à Madrid pour France 24.

france24fr.title: En Guyane, le fléau de la pêche illégale
france24fr.description: En Guyane, la pêche est un secteur en souffrance. Les eaux sont pillées par les bateaux étrangers. Immersion à bord d'un patrouilleur de la Marine nationale, en pleine intervention de lutte contre la pêche clandestine.

france24fr.title: Le Mondial de football, un événement foncièrement géopolitique
france24fr.description: Le coup d’envoi de la Coupe du monde a été donné dans un contexte international particulièrement tendu, marqué par de nombreux conflits et des relations parfois compliquées entre les trois pays hôtes : les États-Unis, le Canada et le Mexique. La compétition permettra-t-elle de confirmer l’idée souvent défendue par la FIFA selon laquelle le football est le sport le plus fédérateur au monde ? Éléments de réponse avec Florian Brejon, directeur général associé de l’agence d’information News Tank Foo

france24fr.title: Femmes arrêtées en Afghanistan : la manifestation à Herat n'a pas eu lieu
france24fr.description: Selon des journalistes de l'AFP, des Afghans ont renoncé vendredi à manifester à Herat en soutien à des femmes arrêtées par la police des mœurs, en raison de l'important dispositif de sécurité déployé par les autorités talibanes. Des appels à manifester dans l'après-midi, après la prière du vendredi, avaient circulé dans la semaine en protestation contre une vague d'arrestations de femmes accusées de ne pas porter de tchador ou de burqa.

france24fr.title: Affaire Lyhanna : plusieurs plaintes visant le père du suspect refont surface
france24fr.description: La France rend un dernier hommage à Lyhanna ce 12 juin, lors des obsèques de la jeune fille dont la mort a profondément ému le pays. Parallèlement, les enquêteurs ont mis au jour plusieurs plaintes visant le père du principal suspect.

zeit.description: Nach Angaben Pakistans sollen die USA und Iran sich auf ein Friedensabkommen geeinigt haben. Irans Außenminister sagte, dass man einer Einigung so nah wie noch nie sei.

nzz.description: Karim Bouamrane führt seit Wochen einen erbitterten Kleinkrieg gegen eine Fast-Food-Kette. Dadurch wurde der Bürgermeister aus der Pariser Banlieue im ganzen Land bekannt. Nun will er bei der Präsidentschaftswahl 2027 antreten.

nzz.description: Prinzessin Bajrakitiyabha lag nach einem Infarkt dreieinhalb Jahre im Koma. Sie war beliebt und galt als wichtige Bezugsperson des thailändischen Königs. Am Donnerstagabend starb sie – und offenbarte ein Königshaus in der Krise.

letemps.description:

spiegel.title: Arbeitslos als Unternehmensberater: »Behaltet euren Job, egal, wie scheiße der ist«
spiegel.description: Trotz Promotion und Netzwerk: Ein Unternehmensberater aus München bewirbt sich seit Mitte 2024 auf Hunderte Stellen und bekommt kaum Rückmeldungen. Hier erzählt der 38-Jährige, warum er genervt auf Ratschläge reagiert.

spiegel.title: Arbeitslos als Akademiker: Vom IT-Studium direkt ins Bürgergeld
spiegel.description: Till Ritzert absolvierte einen IT-Studiengang, jetzt findet er keinen Job. 117 Bewerbungen hat er schon geschrieben, die meisten auf Stellen als Softwareentwickler. Wie der 27-Jährige mit dem Berufseinstieg kämpft.

spiegel.title: Arbeitslos im Alter: »Ich will arbeiten, aber niemand gibt mir eine Chance«
spiegel.description: Mehr als 30 Jahre Erfahrung im Personalwesen – trotzdem laufen alle Bewerbungen ins Leere: Silke Lehnert bewirbt sich seit Monaten vergeblich auf neue Stellen. Hier erzählt die 62-Jährige, was sie jetzt anders machen will.

spiegel.title: Klima: Türkei und Australien schlagen weltweite Elektrifizierungsquote von 35 Prozent vor
spiegel.description: Es gibt noch Fortschritte in der globalen Klimapolitik. Die Türkei und Australien wagen einen Vorstoß, der auch die Deutschen zum Nachdenken über ihr Energiesystem bringen könnte.

spiegel.title: René Benko: Ex-Milliardär muss voraussichtlich wieder vor Gericht
spiegel.description: Zweimal wurde René Benko bereits verurteilt. Nun muss der ehemalige Signa-Chef wohl erneut vor Gericht. Es geht um ein Jagdgewehr, getäuschte Investoren – und auch Benkos Ehefrau.

spiegel.title: News des Tages: SpaceX an der Börse, das West-Nil-Virus, David Hockney gestorben.
spiegel.description: Die Aktie von Elon Musks Weltraumfirma SpaceX feiert an der Nasdaq ihr Handelsdebüt. Das West-Nil-Virus ist jetzt in Berlin heimisch. Und der große Maler David Hockney ist tot. Das ist die Lage am Freitagabend.

spiegel.title: Jane Fonda und Trumps 80. Geburtstag: Gegenaktion zum Käfigkampf in New York
spiegel.description: Der US-Präsident wünscht sich zu seinem 80. Geburtstag Käfigkämpfe vor dem Weißen Haus. Jane Fonda will das nicht einfach hinnehmen. In New York leitet die Schauspielerin deswegen eine Gegenveranstaltung.

spiegel.title: Buckelwal Timmy: Rettungsversuch kostet das Landwirtschaftsministerium rund 50.000 Euro
spiegel.description: Der Rettungsversuch des Wals war ein Millionenprojekt, getragen von zwei Vermögenden. Doch auch das Landwirtschaftsministerium von Till Backhaus hatte Kosten – unter anderem für einen »Wäscheservice«.

spiegel.title: Bundesjugendspiele: »SchülerInnen müssen verstehen, dass Verlieren zum Wettkampf dazugehört«
spiegel.description: Um die Bundesjugendspiele ist seit ihrer Reform eine Debatte entbrannt. Sie seien zu soft, es gehe nicht mehr um Leistung, heißt es. Nun wollen manche Bundesländer das ändern. Ein Sportpädagoge erklärt, was das bedeutet.

spiegel.title: Klez.e, neues Album »Einmal mehr mit Dir gegen die Furcht«: Baustelle der Hoffnung
spiegel.description: Klez.e sind die beste Band, die klingt wie The Cure, ohne The Cure zu sein. Auf ihrem neuen Album geben sich die Berliner Melancholiker überraschend zuversichtlich. Diese neuen Songs sollten Sie hören!

spiegel.title: WM 2026: Die Stadien in Kanada, den USA und Mexiko im Überblick
spiegel.description: Der Schauplatz des Tores mit der »Hand Gottes«, Thomas Müllers neue Heimat, Rudi Völlers Hitzeerinnerung: Hier zeigen wir die WM-Arenen in Kanada, den USA und Mexiko in 3D-Videos und erzählen Besonderheiten.

spiegel.title: Olivia Rodrigo: Wann entflieht sie ihrem Märchenschloss?
spiegel.description: US-Sängerin Olivia Rodrigo ist mit 23 Jahren auf dem Höhepunkt ihrer Karriere. Sie feiert Chart-Hits und zählt Stars wie Robert Smith zu ihren Freunden. Und doch wirkt sie beim Interview in London plötzlich sehr einsam.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: Friedrich Merz kündigt Geburtstagsgeschenk für Trump an
spiegel.description: Zu seinem 80. Geburtstag bekommt Donald Trump einen Käfigkampf – und Geschenke aus Deutschland. Kanzler Friedrich Merz schickt einen handschriftlichen Brief und kündigt eine Überraschung an.

spiegel.title: »Fifa«-Spiel zur WM 2026 auf Netflix im Test: Das taugt das neue »Fifa World Cup«
spiegel.description: Kurze Matches, kaum Optionen, Handys als Controller: Netflix und die Fifa haben ein Videospiel veröffentlicht. Das Beste daran ist eine Hommage an die alten »Fifa«-Games von EA Sports.

spiegel.title: Trump als Mangafigur Naruto: Warum Japan sich über ein KI-Video aufregt
spiegel.description: Mal zeigt er sich als Jesus, mal als Papst: Donald Trump ist bekannt für seine absurden KI-Videos. Dass er sich nun als Manga-Held Naruto inszeniert, empört viele Japaner. Diese Figur ist das genaue Gegenteil von ihm.

spiegel.title: Schweiz: SVP-Initiative zur Bevölkerungsobergrenze verunsichert Zuwanderer
spiegel.description: An diesem Wochenende stimmt die Schweiz über einen Vorschlag der rechtspopulistischen SVP ab: Die Einwohnerzahl soll auf zehn Millionen beschränkt werden. Was das für Deutsche dort – und für Europa – bedeuten würde.

spiegel.title: AfD-Entsandte im Parlament: Nach dem Auftritt im Bundestag kam es zum Polizeieinsatz im Hotel
spiegel.description: Ein rechtsextremer Vorfall überschattet ein Treffen von Jugendlichen im Bundestag. Nach SPIEGEL-Informationen kam es am Rande der Veranstaltung zu einem gewalttätigen Vorfall. Im Mittelpunkt: Entsandte der AfD.

spiegel.title: Meta: Probleme bei WhatsApp, Facebook und Instagram sorgen für Ausfälle
spiegel.description: Wer im Internet chatten und kommunizieren möchte, kommt an den Diensten des Meta-Konzerns nur schwer vorbei. Seit Freitagnachmittag berichten zahlreiche Nutzer von Problemen.

observador.title: Fogo em Vieira do Minho com mais de 100 operacionais
observador.description: O fogo em Vieira do Minho alastra em mato numa encosta de difícil acesso, sem ameaçar habitações. A reativação do incêndio de Terras de Bouro foi dominada pelas 17h30.

observador.title: Putin promete rede de satélites superior a Starlink
observador.description: O impedimento do uso da Starlink pela Rússia tem permitido ataques de drones ucranianos e recuperação de território. No Dia Nacional, Putin afirmou que rede de satélites russa está a ser ampliada.

observador.title: As notícias das 18h
observador.description: As notícias na Rádio Observador. Aconteça o que acontecer.

observador.title: PSD promete apoio na eleição se PS insistir em Luísa Neto
observador.description: Depois da votação insuficiente da provedora da Justiça, Hugo Soares disse colocar "todo o empenho" caso o PS repita a indicação de Luísa Neto. Cargo está por preencher desde o início da legislatura.

observador.title: Ministra diz que reduzir lixo é questão ambiental e ética
observador.description: Maria da Graça Carvalho anunciou alternativas aos sacos plásticos leves para 2027. Portugal pagou 600 ME em multas à UE e deposita 54% dos resíduos em aterro, meta é 10% até 2035.

observador.title: Influencers condenados por violar e filmar menor
observador.description: Os quatro influencers tinham milhares de seguidores nas redes sociais e um dos vídeos do crime foi visto mais de 32 mil vezes, apesar de ninguém ter alertado as autoridades.

observador.title: Autarcas do PSD pedem revisão da Lei das Finanças Locais
observador.description: Os Autarcas Social-Democratas preparam proposta temática para o Congresso do PSD de 20 e 21 de junho em Anadia, com foco na revisão da Lei das Finanças Locais e eleitoral.

observador.title: "Eu era a primeira opção." A apresentação de Marco Silva
observador.description: O treinador confirmou que está prestes a começar o "maior desafio da carreira", mostrou vontade de ser "dominador", reconheceu lado "emocional" na decisão e garantiu que a primeira opção de Rui Costa.

observador.title: Quem são os quatro novos juízes do Tribunal Constitucional?
observador.description: PSD escolheu um secretário de Estado de Passos Coelho e uma professora catedrática de direito. PS indicou filha de antigo PGR. Juiz indicado pelo Chega é descrito como “moderado e equilibrado”.

observador.title: Seguro deixa alerta sobre uso da IA na na justiça
observador.description: António José Seguro discursava na sessão de abertura de uma cerimónia comemorativa dos 100 anos da Ordem dos Advogados, na Aula Magna da Reitoria da Universidade de Lisboa.

observador.title: Renault e Mercedes investem forte no sector militar
observador.description: Com a indústria automóvel a atravessar uma crise, Renault e Mercedes optam por diversificar a sua estratégia. Os franceses vão produzir drones voadores e os alemães sistemas para os abater.

observador.title: Fogo  corta EN15 e obriga a evacuar motel
observador.description: O fogo deflagrou esta tarde em Gondomar e mobilizou mais de 100 operacionais. Não há feridos nem casas ameaçadas, mas a EN15 está cortada.

observador.title: Pequim detém investigador norte-americano por espionagem
observador.description: Caso é considerado invulgar uma vez que detenções de cidadãos norte-americanos por acusações de espionagem são relativamente raras na China. O investigador terá sido detido a 3 de junho.

observador.title: PS vota moções setoriais a 28 de junho
observador.description: A reunião, em Lisboa, arranca com uma intervenção de José Luís Carneiro. Regionalização, integração europeia e imigração estão entre os temas em discussão.

observador.title: Ford: 250.000 carros na revisão por falha no motor
observador.description: Os veículos são modelos fabricados entre 2012 e 2018. A falha no filtro de carburação pode fazer o motor parar sem aviso. Solução passa por atualização de software gratuita.

observador.title: Livre lança contraproposta ao pacote laboral
observador.description: Tal como o Chega, Livre também propõe reposição dos 25 dias de férias abolidos pela troika. Sugere criação de fundo para transição tecnológica que taxe a automação e insiste na semana de quatro dias.

observador.title: Mundial 2026. Quem veste as seleções fora do relvado
observador.description: Dos óculos de Cristiano Ronaldo, passando pelos motivos étnicos da Costa do Marfim e a alfaiataria de luxo do Japão: o airport style dos jogadores neste arranque do Campeonato Mundial de Futebol.

observador.title: SpaceX começa a negociar em bolsa acima do preço da oferta
observador.description: A SpaceX vendeu as suas ações a 135 dólares. No arranque da negociação em bolsa vale, cada ação, 150 dólares, uma valorização de 11% face ao preço de colocação.

republika.title: Guerra in Iran. Il premier pakistano: “Raggiunto un testo concordato dell’accordo di pace Iran-Usa”
republika.description: Attesa per l'ok di Khamenei. Pasdaran frenano: "Firma a Ginevra? Illusione americana". Per Reuters possibile firma del memorandum domenica con Ghalibaf e Vance che sottolinea: “L’Iran non riceverà fondi in automatico”. Trump: “Abbiamo vinto senza Ue”. Axios, aerei Usa verso Europa per firma intesa. Nell’accordo cessate il fuoco per 60 giorni anche in Libano”.

republika.title: La diretta RepIdee arriva in piazza per una serata di politica e spettacolo: dai sindaci a Recalcati, chiude Ditonellapiaga
republika.description: Tanti appuntamenti con la politica al centro del dibattito. Tra gli ospiti della giornata Silvia Salis, Roberto Gualtieri, Massimo Recalcati, Luisa Ranieri e Ditonellapiaga

republika.title: Problema tecnico sull’aereo del papa: il pontefice rientra con il Falcon di re Filippo
republika.description: Accompagnato in aeroporto dal reale spagnolo, il pontefice sarebbe dovuto arrivare a Roma alle 20.40. Iberia ha comunicato in una nota che il problema "non può essere riparato immediatamente”

republika.title: Caso Garlasco, Alberto Stasi verso l’uscita dal carcere e l’affidamento in prova
republika.description: Il parere positivo della Procura Generale per l'affidamento ai servizi sociali presso la società in cui lavora

republika.title: Il caso dello stadio vuoto al Mondiale: i numeri della Fifa che non convincono e i costi folli
republika.description: A Guadalajara per Corea del Sud-Repubblica Ceca tanti posti liberi sugli spalti. Ma per le fonti ufficiali c’era il tutto esaurito

republika.title: Avvelenate di Pietracatella, indagata per favoreggiamento un’amica di famiglia dei Di Vita
republika.description: La donna, sentita più volte dagli inquirenti, avrebbe negato tensioni e litigi all’interno del nucleo delle due donne avvelenate di cui sarebbe stata invece a conoscenza. Smentita dalle chat estratte dai telefoni

republika.title: SpaceX sbarca al Nasdaq, Musk suona la campanella a distanza: “Verso Marte e oltre”
republika.description: Nella sede della borsa si presenta anche Maye Musk, la madre dell’uomo più ricco del mondo. In centinaia davanti al maxi schermo di Times Square

republika.title: Ferrovie, l’ad Donnarumma: “Un’estate ad alta concentrazione di cantieri, ma viaggiare si può”
republika.description: L’amministratore delegato ospite di Repubblica delle Idee: “Non siamo fanalino di coda. Frecciarossa puntuali, ecco i dati”

republika.title: Yamal fa la spesa in un supermercato negli Usa senza essere riconosciuto. Era già successo a Messi
republika.description: La stella della Spagna ripresa tra le corsie, sui social la foto con il carrello pieno. Il precedente del fuoriclasse argentino, a Miami, nel 2023

republika.title: L’Aquila, bimba di tre anni dimenticata per ore sullo scuolabus. Il papà: “Sfiorata la tragedia”
republika.description: A lanciare l’allarme a Pizzoli la famiglia della piccola, ora la procura ha aperto un fascicolo

republika.title: Nicole Minetti, caso (quasi) chiuso: “Ordine di esecuzione della pena revocato dopo la grazia”
republika.description: L’ultima parola ai giudici che devono esprimersi sul “non luogo a provvedere” nei confronti dell’ex consigliera regionale, condannata a 3 anni e 11 mesi

republika.title: Infantino deride l’Italia: “Magari con il Mondiale a 64 squadre si qualificherà”
republika.description: La battuta infelice del presidente della Fifa sulla mancata partecipazione degli azzurri al torneo. Il ministro Abodi: “Voglio parlargli, sono affermazioni che mi lasciano perplesso”

republika.title: Gentiloni: “L'Europa sotto assedio. Trump mi chiese cosa fosse l'Ue. Un no a Kiev sarebbe inaccettabile”
republika.description: A Repubblica delle Idee le riflessioni sulle sfide per l’Unione

republika.title: Ventimiglia, ritrovati i corpi senza vita dei due ragazzi dispersi
republika.description: Mercoledì erano spariti tra le onde Whalid Sobi, 19 anni, ed Ewerton Bernardo Dos Santos, 25 anni

republika.title: De Pascale a RepIdee: “La coalizione metta in campo subito un programma e una leadership”
republika.description: Il presidente della Regione Emilia-Romagna intervistato dal caporedattore di Bologna Giovanni Egidio. Sul centrodestra: “Vannacci? Le stesse cose le hanno dette Meloni e Salvini”

republika.title: Monopattini, ecco tutte le regole: si può guidare in due? Il casco è obbligatorio?
republika.description: Nel 2026 il il Codice della Strada ha introdotto regole più rigide

republika.title: Un elicottero precipita sul Lago Maggiore, un morto e tre feriti
republika.description: La vittima è Adrian Bryner: l’incidente è avvenuto a terra e non in acqua

republika.title: Repubblica delle Idee a Bologna, il direttore Orfeo: “Festeggiamo mezzo secolo e scriviamo insieme una storia di futuro”
republika.description: Al via la nuova edizione. Sul palco con Laura Pertici anche il sindaco Matteo Lepore, il presidente della Regione Michele De Pascale e Giovanni Egidio

nyt.title: Elon Musk Becomes World’s First Trillionaire as SpaceX Stock Begins Trading
nyt.description: With SpaceX shares soaring on their first day of trading, the world’s richest person crossed another milestone — one with 13 digits.

nyt.title: A Dangerous Limbo Leaves Iran, and the World, Between Peace and War
nyt.description: Since announcing a nominal cease-fire two months ago, Iran, Israel and the U.S. have remained locked in low-intensity violence that has become a new normal.

nyt.title: The World Is Draining Oil Reserves, Raising Pressure for a Peace Deal
nyt.description: The amount of oil and fuel stored by businesses and governments has fallen sharply since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran.

nyt.title: Despite Talk of an Iran Peace Deal, Lebanon’s War Grinds On
nyt.description: Israeli strikes on Friday left Lebanon out of sync with a cautious optimism taking hold elsewhere in the Middle East.

nyt.title: FISA, a Key U.S. Spying Power, Is Expiring. What Does That Mean for Foreign Surveillance?
nyt.description: Top officials and some lawmakers say letting a powerful spying authority expire on Saturday will leave the United States dangerously blind. But surveillance can still continue.

nyt.title: David Hockney, Who Restored the Human Form to Art, Dies at 88
nyt.description: His colorful figurative paintings were both conservative and iconoclastic, defying the dominant abstract schools of the mid-20th century.

nyt.title: Framing David Hockney’s Greatest Art
nyt.description: Whether in Los Angeles, in his native England or traveling the world, the artist always reinvented the world he saw, with psychological insight.

nyt.title: David Hockney’s Sense of Style Never Wavered
nyt.description: The painter David Hockney’s clothes roared with mirth and maximalism.

nyt.title: Inside Cesar Chavez’s Labor Union, Women Faced a Culture of Sexual Abuse
nyt.description: Many of the women who helped lead the fight for Latino civil rights say they were quietly waging their own battles with harassment, misogyny and sexual assault inside the powerful United Farm Workers union.

nyt.title: U.S. Plan Is Said to Pull a Third of Fighter Jets It Provides NATO for Europe
nyt.description: The plan, outlined by officials and in a written document, provides rare clarity about the extent to which the Trump administration intends to reduce its commitment to NATO.

nyt.title: After Senate Loss, Cornyn Predicts ‘Miserable’ Final Two Years for Trump
nyt.description: In his first extensive interview since his defeat by a Trump-backed challenger, the Texas Republican said the Senate was in for a “bumpy ride” as he and others flex new political freedom.

nyt.title: Can Democrats Overcome G.O.P. Gerrymandering?
nyt.description: Our chief political analyst, Nate Cohn, who writes The Tilt newsletter, looks at the Republicans’ advantage in the House of Representatives after partisan redistricting. To win the House, how much of the popular vote would Democrats need to win?

nyt.title: Rick Jackson, Georgia Governor Candidate, Is Also a Film Producer Battling the IRS
nyt.description: Rick Jackson, a billionaire, wants to be Georgia’s next governor. But the I.R.S. has questioned how his low-budget movies turned into tax windfalls.

nyt.title: AIPAC Wants Democrats to Back Israel. Instead, They’re Turning on AIPAC.
nyt.description: Once the guardian of the bipartisan pro-Israel consensus, it is now a polarizing force in the party.

nyt.title: Suspect in Fatal Shooting Is Dead After a Standoff in Midland, Texas, Officials Say
nyt.description: The man was confirmed to be dead after he had barricaded himself in a building in Midland, following an earlier shooting on Friday that killed one person and injured at least 11 others.

nyt.title: She Was Dying of Cancer. How Should She Live?
nyt.description: Thanks to new treatments, some patients with Stage 4 cancer are living longer — leaving them in limbo for years.

nyt.title: Trump’s D.C. Renovations, HGTV Style
nyt.description: President Trump brings a particular brand of reality TV-style renovations to the nation’s capital.

nyt.title: Fact-Check: Trump’s Claims About His Arch, Reflecting Pool Repairs and Other Renovation Projects
nyt.description: President Trump has made false or exaggerated claims of a Civil War-era push for a triumphal arch, hundreds of millions spent on repairs on the Reflecting Pool, and an absence of working fountains.

npr.title: China arrests a U.S. scholar with a history of Myanmar activism, suspected of spying
npr.description: China's government said Min Zin, who heads a think tank focused on Myanmar, was detained on suspicion of engaging in "espionage and endangering Chinese national security."

npr.title: Trump cancels further Iran strikes. And, U.S. men's soccer takes on Paraguay
npr.description: Trump canceled new Iran strikes and signaled that a peace deal could come soon, but Iran says it hasn't been finalized. And, the U.S. men's soccer team plays its first 2026 World Cup match today.

npr.title: She waited decades for Scotland to make the World Cup. At 93, she'll cheer in person
npr.description: Moira Brown, perhaps the oldest of Scotland's Tartan Army of soccer fans, will be in Boston when Scotland's team plays against Haiti on June 13. "I'm the luckiest person in this world," she says.

npr.title: Ousted South Korean President Yoon given prison term for drone flights over Pyongyang
npr.description: South Korea's ousted President Yoon Suk Yeol and his former defense minister were sentenced to 30 years in prison Friday in a case alleging Yoon ordered drone flights over Pyongyang in 2024 to heighten tensions with North Korea and justify declaring martial law at home.

npr.title: The Teddy Bear Doctor treats stuffies in need of care
npr.description: Ruth Hasman's home in British Columbia is known as the teddy bear hospital -- a place where stuffies in need of repair receive the TLC they need.

npr.title: Trump now says a peace deal will be announced 'soon,' cancels further strikes
npr.description: President Trump had previously been amping up his rhetoric against Iran.

npr.title: Taiwan opposition leader says Xi meeting avoided 'reunification' talk
npr.description: Cheng's comments come as Taiwan awaits approval on a $14 billion arms package from the U.S., and as uncertainty lingers over Washington's long-term commitment to the island's defense.

npr.title: Japan reactor restart sparks fresh fears over nuclear waste storage
npr.description: The reboot highlights a dire problem for the country's nuclear program. Japan is running out of space to store spent nuclear fuel and lacks plans for radioactive waste disposal.

npr.title: Greetings from a Seoul museum, where Buddhist masterpieces offer calm away from city bustle
npr.description: The National Museum of Korea is home to the Room of Quiet Contemplation, which features two of South Korea's most treasured artworks: gilt-bronze bodhisattva statues from the sixth and seventh centuries.

npr.title: U.S. launches second day of Iran strikes. And, World Cup facts to know before kickoff
npr.description: The U.S. launched air strikes on Iran for a second consecutive day. And, the World Cup kicks off today in Mexico City, where tensions threaten to disrupt events.

elpais.title: Todas las selecciones del Mundial 2026 en Estados Unidos, Canadá y México
elpais.description: La competición con más equipos de la historia pone en juego a 48 combinados nacionales durante cinco semanas. Consulte aquí todos los detalles

elpais.title: El juez del ‘caso Plus Ultra’ abre una pieza separada para investigar a Zapatero por delito fiscal y contrabando por las joyas halladas en su despacho
elpais.description: Calama recibió este jueves la tasación por 1.323.915 euros de las piezas requisadas al expresidente por la UDEF

elpais.title: El valor de las joyas de Zapatero: desde baratijas “sin valor” hasta un collar de 278.000 euros
elpais.description: El informe pericial realizado por la joyería Ansorena y el Instituto Gemológico Español recoge alhajas con diamantes, zafíros, esmeraldas y rubíes

elpais.title: Dirigentes del PSOE reprochan a Zapatero que diese un valor inferior a las joyas: “Nos está arrastrando con él”
elpais.description: En medio de la inquietud en las filas socialistas, Ferraz remite a la declaración del expresidente la próxima semana en la Audiencia Nacional

elpais.title: El Ejecutivo de Ayuso condiciona la tarjeta de transporte al empadronamiento y excluye a miles de usuarios, sobre todo migrantes y estudiantes
elpais.description: La Comunidad hace obligatorio el documento tras las colas de extranjeros para usar el título para demostrar su arraigo en la regularización del Gobierno central y calcula en 200.000 a los usuarios afectados

elpais.title: SpaceX se estrena en Bolsa a 150 dólares por acción, con una subida del 11%
elpais.description: La valoración de la empresa roza los dos billones de dólares. “SpaceX trata de sacar la ficción de la ciencia ficción y crear un futuro emocionante”, asegura Elon Musk, que se convierte en el primer billonario

elpais.title: Última hora de la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán, en directo | Pakistán afirma que Irán y Estados Unidos han alcanzado un acuerdo de paz

phys-org.title: Landscape water velocities across Europe reshape nitrogen pollution risk under climate change
phys-org.description: Nitrate pollution is a growing global environmental challenge due to the extensive use of fertilizer. A study published in Science, led by the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries (IGB) with the Helmholtz Center for Environmental Research (UFZ), shows that both the amount of water moving through landscapes and how fast it moves play a key role in nitrogen pollution risk.

phys-org.title: Nuclear clocks tick for the first time
phys-org.description: Two independent research teams have achieved a longstanding goal in physics: building a working nuclear clock. The devices, developed by Beichen Huang and colleagues at Tsinghua University and by Luca Toscani De Col and colleagues at the Vienna Center for Quantum Science and Technology in Austria, exploit the nucleus of a thorium-229 atom to keep time with extraordinary precision—possibly surpassing even the best atomic clocks available today.

phys-org.title: Carbon dioxide unlocks safer oxidation chemistry under room-temperature conditions

phys-org.title: Horse owners' personality and attachment style shape how they interact with and care for their horses
phys-org.description: A new study shows that horse owners' psychological characteristics, including their attachment styles and personality traits, are systematically linked to how frequently they ride, train, and spend quality time with their horses, as well as the equipment they choose to use. The findings offer new insights into how human psychology shapes horse welfare and management.

phys-org.title: Engineered bacterium turns potato starch into biodegradable plastic in 24 hours
phys-org.description: Every year, hundreds of millions of tons of petrochemical-based plastics are produced, much of which ends up in the environment or is incinerated. This exacerbates greenhouse gas emissions and the environmental crisis caused by plastic pollution. Scientists from the universities of Exeter and Lund reviewed global evidence and found 100 dragonfly and damselfly species that migrate, and a further 85 possible migratory species. phys-org.title: AI tracks missing hydrogen atoms in crystals with 97% success rate
phys-org.description: Artificial intelligence is often used to generate images. In research, specialized AI models are used for scientific applications—for example, to predict the positions of atoms in materials. The MatterGen model developed by Microsoft can generate complex crystal structures from just a few pieces of information—which atoms should be present and in what proportions—and researchers can then use these structures for computer simulations of new materials.

phys-org.title: A cornerstone of Milky Way history may need rewriting with evidence of multiple ancient mergers
phys-org.description: Astronomers may have uncovered new details about one of the Milky Way's most important ancient collisions. Using data from the Dark Energy Spectroscopic Instrument (DESI) and a new clustering algorithm, researchers have found evidence suggesting the famous Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus structure (GSE) has a far more complicated origin than previously thought.

phys-org.title: New findings complete first evolutionary history of all living millipede orders, dating back 460 million years
phys-org.description: Long before vertebrates walked on land, millipedes had the place to themselves. Hundreds of millions of years before dinosaurs arrived, these early decomposers were helping establish Earth's terrestrial ecosystems. But despite their ancient history, scientists still hadn't fully unraveled their evolutionary story.

phys-org.title: Photo: Hubble and Webb offer new view of Black Eye Galaxy
phys-org.description: This March 20, 2026, image of Messier 64, or the Black Eye Galaxy, is a composite view from NASA's Hubble Space Telescope and James Webb Space Telescope. It shows Messier 64 captured at near- and mid-infrared wavelengths by Webb, while Hubble's image shows the galaxy in ultraviolet, visible, and near-infrared light.

phys-org.title: Hubble captures galaxy swarm with lensed arcs from early universe
phys-org.description: Looking somewhat like a swarm of bees returning to their hive, this NASA Hubble Space Telescope image features the galaxy cluster MACS0329-0211. Galaxy clusters like MACS0329-0211 are important signposts in the story of how the structure of the universe evolved, and are the ultimate telescopic lenses, placing gravitationally lensed galaxies from the earliest stages of the universe into our view.

phys-org.title: Meltwater is causing Antarctic glaciers to flow faster toward the ocean
phys-org.description: In a new study, Professor Shin Sugiyama of Hokkaido University and his team have directly confirmed for the first time that water from melting snow and ice, or meltwater, found at the surface of a glacier can drain to its base, causing glaciers in Antarctica to speed up and move toward the ocean.

It releases a fruity nectar scent to attract flies and other insects. After they land in the trap, tiny hairs are triggered and the leaves shut with impressive speed.

undark.title: Promising ‘Liquid Biopsies’ May Not Be Ready for Primetime
undark.description: Multi-cancer early detection tests seek to spot cancer from a single blood draw. Enabling earlier cancer diagnoses could help save lives and limit the need for invasive interventions. But while the tests are promising, physicians have expressed doubt about routine use by low-risk and asymptomatic individuals.

undark.title: Book Review: How Radio Astronomy Made the Invisible Visible
undark.description: According to astronomer Emma Chapman’s revelatory “The Echoing Universe,” the history of radio astronomy is filled with surprises that have revealed parts of the universe that would otherwise remain hidden and invisible — DIY instruments, secrets accidentally uncovered, and persistent connections to Earth.

undark.title: Risk Aversion in Science Stifles Innovation
undark.description: Does the scientific enterprise play it too safe? C. Brandon Ogbunu argues that risk-taking in science involves a willingness to reflect on the processes and incentives of the profession — and to dramatically overhaul them if they do not work. Only then can true scientific innovation take shape.

undark.title: A Peptide, a Secretive Scientist, and a Debate Over Evidence
undark.description: Access to unapproved peptides like BPC-157 has become a cause célèbre for the MAHA movement. Undark contributing editor Sara Talpos digs into the untold history of BPC-157 and its long journey from the scientific margins to the center of a debate over U.S. drug regulation.

undark.title: Book Review: Within Our Cells, the Miracle of Constant Mutation
undark.description: Our cells are constantly mutating in a battle for the survival of the fittest that is raging inside us daily, Roxanne Khamsi writes in “Beyond Inheritance.” Many of these mutations are harmless, others are cellular deviants that lead to disease, and remarkably, some can actually self-correct.

undark.title: The Six-Week Postpartum Checkup Comes Too Late
undark.description: In the U.S., maternity care generally ends with a checkup scheduled six weeks after giving birth. This single doctor’s appointment may be efficient for billing and discharge protocols, but the timing reflects the structure of the health care system more than the reality of maternal recovery.

undark.title: Book Review:  The Case for Making Data-Driven Decisions
undark.description: In “Beyond Belief: How Evidence Shows What Really Works,” science journalist Helen Pearson profiles a group of people working in medicine and other fields who became leaders of the worldwide evidence movement, which encourages the use of data from rigorous research to direct treatments, policies, and plans.

undark.title: What the Hantavirus Story Reveals About Medical Mistrust
undark.description: The reaction to an outbreak of hantavirus on a cruise ship reveals a story about mistrust in medicine and public health. In the U.S., hantavirus disproportionately kills Native Americans. A doctor who works at a hospital on Navajo Nation writes that such mistrust always lands hardest on the most vulnerable.

undark.title: Book Review: The Mind-Boggling Science of Enormous Numbers
undark.description: In “Huge Numbers: A Story of Counting Ambitiously, From 4½ to Fish 7,” mathematician Richard Elwes shows off his love of all things numeric, and, in particular, shines a spotlight on some of the largest numbers humans have ever contemplated, and the much larger numbers that await those who seek them out.

undark.title: When Scientific Arguments Obscure Moral Ones, Democracy Suffers
undark.description: The Pentagon’s new vaccine policy values individual choice over public health. Which of these values should be prioritized is a legitimate subject for democratic debate. But when experts respond to moral arguments animating policy decisions by reiterating facts, it undermines debate and fuels divisiveness.

proj-syn.title: Europeans Are the G7’s Grownups
proj-syn.description: Slowly but surely, the European Union is taking steps to reduce its current-account surplus and direct more of its substantial savings into domestic investment and growth. Unfortunately, at the G7 Summit in France this month, the United States will refuse to address global imbalances, including its own.

proj-syn.title: Modi Is Rigging Indian Democracy
proj-syn.description: Under the guise of routine voter-roll maintenance, India’s Election Commission has purged tens of millions of voters, disproportionately affecting opposition strongholds, the poor, and Muslim minorities. The result is an electoral system increasingly designed to favor the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party.

proj-syn.title: Learning to Govern a Fragmented World
proj-syn.description: As the postwar multilateral order gives way to a multipolar and more contested world, global governance must adapt or risk irrelevance. The upcoming G7 summit offers a unique opportunity to champion a coalition-based approach that translates shared interests into collective action.

proj-syn.title: Cognition for Sale
proj-syn.description: AI is doing what no previous technology could, turning tacit human knowledge into a product that can be extracted, priced, and distributed at scale. Yet the same technology that democratizes cognitive labor may also weaken the human capacities on which complex societies depend.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech Gets Bigger
proj-syn.description: Recent stock-market gyrations are a reminder of just how dependent the United States and global economies have become on investors’ seemingly insatiable appetite for tech stocks. Even if a major correction is in the offing, however, it will not happen before SpaceX’s massive initial public offering draws in yet more leveraged investment, nor will it destroy the market power of the other tech giants that have spent years perfecting anti-competitive tactics that largely escape regulators’ purvi

proj-syn.title: The Democrats Need a Story, Not More Lists
proj-syn.description: Whereas Donald Trump has offered voters a clear and compelling narrative, Democrats have provided only vague aspirations and long lists of policies. To win over voters—rather than scrounging protest votes—they must articulate a compelling economic vision, with wage-led growth as its foundation.

proj-syn.title: What if Europe Loses Access to Its Climate Data?
proj-syn.description: The European Green Deal runs on data, from corporate disclosures to climate-risk analyses and decarbonization pathways. But much of this data feeds platforms and tools developed outside the European Union, which could threaten the bloc’s climate agenda and even its foundational values.

proj-syn.title: Raising Interest Rates Won’t Stabilize African Inflation
proj-syn.description: Monetary tightening in Africa would not only fail to rein in inflation; it would raise the cost of productive investment, suppress growth, and hamper the continent's much-needed structural transformation. A better strategy would focus on accelerating this transformation by channeling finance into productive industries.

proj-syn.title: Peak Oil Demand Has Arrived
proj-syn.description: Amid the disruptions caused by the US/Israeli-Iran war, countries have begun adapting to life with less oil. What started as a supply shock has become a demand story, forcing the energy sector to reconsider one of its most important assumptions: continued growth of global oil demand.

proj-syn.title: The Enduring Enigma of Economic Growth
proj-syn.description: Developing countries have made enormous progress in many of the factors behind growth, reflected in stronger institutions, rising education levels, higher life expectancy, and increased investment rates. Yet income convergence with advanced economies has been painfully slow—and in most cases absent.

proj-syn.title: Is the US Stock Market Too Big?
proj-syn.description: With China and India having grown so fast as to compensate for the underperformance of their fellow BRICS (Brazil, Russia, and South Africa), the center of gravity in the global economy continues to shift eastward. The question now is whether—and when—equity valuations will reflect this underlying reality.

proj-syn.title: Brazil’s Bad Vibes
proj-syn.description: A government that abandons structural agendas whenever sentiment turns negative will still be managing sentiment four years later—with nothing to show for it. Brazil’s “vibecession” is a real problem for the current government; but winning the news cycle is not a real solution.

proj-syn.title: Negotiating With the Antichrist
proj-syn.description: Apocalyptic thinking is seeping into the political discourse, with figures like Peter Thiel, Pete Hegseth, and Aleksandr Dugin portraying political differences as struggles between good and evil. When rivals become mortal enemies, the instruments of politics and diplomacy cannot work.

proj-syn.title: Why Is Europe’s Economy Falling Short?
proj-syn.description: For much of the postwar era, European policymakers have prioritized stability and predictability over fostering breakthrough innovation. Today, as the United States and China compete for AI dominance, a stagnant Europe is struggling to regain its place at the technological frontier.

proj-syn.title: Big Tech’s Shadow Market Power
proj-syn.description: Big Tech firms are amassing market power through strategies that bypass current rules for oversight, investigation, and intervention. Unless and until regulators account for the full scope and scale of these strategies, Silicon Valley’s dominance will remain unchallenged.

proj-syn.title: The AI Revolution Mirrors the Green Transition
proj-syn.description: The need for massive upfront investments and the likelihood of significant job displacement imply remarkable parallels between the AI buildout and the green transition. In both cases, the state has an important role to play in guiding market forces on behalf of the public good.

proj-syn.title: Where Is China’s Trillion-Dollar Trade Surplus Going?
proj-syn.description: Whereas China’s trade surplus used to be absorbed largely by the central bank and channeled into official reserves, it is now being redeployed by private actors in search of yield. This indicates China’s progress on financial deepening and underscores markets' increasingly central role in shaping the economy.
